subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Supine hypotensive syndrome; gynecologic tumor epidemiology
vignette: A 31-year-old woman at 32 weeks' gestation lies flat on her back for a prolonged examination and suddenly feels lightheaded. Her blood pressure falls to 88/54 mm Hg with a weak pulse. Her symptoms resolve within a minute after she rolls onto her left side.
question: Compression of which pair of vessels by the gravid uterus best explains this presentation?

options.text: Abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava

explanation_correct: Supine hypotensive (aortocaval compression) syndrome occurs after 20 weeks when the gravid uterus compresses the abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava while the patient is supine. This decreases venous return, producing hypotension, and reduces placental perfusion, which can lead to pregnancy loss. It is relieved by the left lateral decubitus position.

explanation_incorrect.A: The renal vessels are not the structures compressed in aortocaval compression syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.B: The superior vena cava lies in the thorax and is not compressed by the gravid uterus; the inferior vena cava is the vessel involved.
explanation_incorrect.C: The celiac trunk and portal vein are not responsible for the reduced venous return and placental perfusion seen here.
explanation_incorrect.E: The common iliac vessels are located lower in the pelvis and are not the classic vessels compressed in this syndrome.

educationalObjective: Supine hypotensive (aortocaval compression) syndrome at >20 weeks: gravid uterus compresses the aorta and IVC, decreasing venous return and placental perfusion; relieved by left lateral decubitus.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Supine hypotensive syndrome; gynecologic tumor epidemiology
vignette: A medical student reviews the epidemiology of the three major gynecologic malignancies in the United States: endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancer. She wants to recall their relative frequency in the US as well as how the ranking differs worldwide.
question: In the United States, which of the following correctly orders these cancers by decreasing incidence?
explanation_correct: In the United States, the incidence of gynecologic cancers is endometrial > ovarian > cervical. Cervical cancer is more common worldwide because of limited screening and HPV vaccination. This US ranking is a commonly tested epidemiologic fact.

explanation_incorrect.B: Cervical cancer is more common worldwide, where screening and vaccination are less available, but it is the least common of the three in the United States.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ovarian cancer has the worst prognosis but is not the most common gynecologic cancer in the US.
explanation_incorrect.D: In the US, ovarian cancer occurs more frequently than cervical cancer, so cervical should be last.
explanation_incorrect.E: This order reflects neither the US incidence (endometrial highest) nor the correct worldwide position of cervical cancer.

educationalObjective: US gynecologic cancer incidence: endometrial > ovarian > cervical; cervical is more common worldwide where screening and HPV vaccination are limited.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Supine hypotensive syndrome; gynecologic tumor epidemiology
vignette: A gynecologic oncologist teaches a class using the 'CEO' mnemonic for the major gynecologic cancers: cervical, endometrial, and ovarian. The mnemonic captures that prognosis goes from best to worst as the typical patient age increases (cervical diagnosed before 45, endometrial around 55, ovarian after 65).
question: Which of the following correctly orders these gynecologic cancers by prognosis from best to worst?
explanation_correct: Prognosis is best for cervical cancer (usually diagnosed before age 45), intermediate for endometrial cancer (around age 55), and worst for ovarian cancer (usually after age 65). The 'CEO' mnemonic—CEOs go from best to worst as they get older—captures both the order and the typical age at diagnosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Ovarian cancer has the worst prognosis and the oldest typical age at diagnosis, so it cannot be placed first.
explanation_incorrect.B: Cervical cancer, diagnosed at the youngest age, has the best prognosis and belongs ahead of endometrial cancer.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ovarian cancer has a worse prognosis than endometrial cancer, so ovarian should be last, not in the middle.
explanation_incorrect.D: Both cervical and ovarian are misplaced; cervical should be first and ovarian last.

educationalObjective: Prognosis: cervical (best, <45 years) > endometrial (~55 years) > ovarian (worst, >65 years) — 'CEOs best to worst as they get older.'
